title: Senior Product Manager
description: <p><strong>Quiénes somos</strong></p><p><strong>Acerca de Fudo</strong></p><p>Somos una startup que combina experiencia en la industria gastronómica y pasión por la tecnología. Todos los días ayudamos a miles de restaurantes a lo largo de Latinoamérica a mejorar su servicio gracias a nuestro software de gestión y aplicaciones móviles. Nuestro sistema es líder en Chile y Argentina y estamos creciendo aceleradamente en México, Colombia y Brasil.</p><p><br></p><p>Nuestro mayor propósito es hacerle la vida más fácil a los emprendedores gastronómicos brindándoles las mejores herramientas para llevar adelante sus negocios y, para eso, necesitamos investigar, lanzar productos y llegar a más usuarios de la mano de un gran equipo.</p><p><br></p><p>Cada persona que nos conforma es crucial, por lo que priorizamos generar una cultura basada en la empatía, la transparencia, las ganas y el compromiso.</p><p><br></p><p><strong>Acerca del equipo</strong></p><p>El equipo de Producto es un equipo en crecimiento que pertenece al área de Tecnología. Trabaja en conjunto con los equipos de Ingeniería y de UX y en estrecho vínculo con el C-level.</p><p><br></p><p><strong>Descripción del rol</strong></p><p>El rol de Product Manager cubre el proceso de definición, desarrollo y evolución de todas las funcionalidades relacionadas a la vertical de back-office dentro de nuestro software, siendo parte de un equipo multidisciplinario, que incluye personas de Ingeniería y Diseño.</p><p><br></p><p><strong>Responsabilidades del rol</strong></p><ul><li>Liderar el roadmap de las funcionalidades de <em>back-office</em> de la plataforma, transformando la gestión administrativa y financiera de los negocios gastronómicos en una experiencia eficiente y automatizada.</li><li>Identificar oportunidades de producto a través de entrevistas con operadores de restaurantes (dueños, gerentes de local, encargados de cocina) y traducirlas en soluciones concretas dentro del ecosistema Fudo.</li><li>Definir métricas de éxito por feature y hacer seguimiento de adopción — con especial foco en usuarios no técnicos que toman decisiones operativas del día a día.</li><li>Colaborar con equipos de UX, ingeniería, soporte y comercial para entregar funcionalidades que reduzcan la fricción en la operación back-office del restaurante.</li><li>Priorizar el backlog balanceando deuda técnica, necesidades de clientes actuales y oportunidades de expansión de producto.</li><li>Gestionar el ciclo completo de desarrollo: discovery, definición, entrega y medición de impacto.</li></ul><p><br></p><p><strong>Experiencia y competencias requeridas</strong></p><ul><li>Experiencia liderando desarrollos de productos tecnológicos.</li><li>Experiencia en productos B2B SaaS, con enfoque en gestión y herramientas de administración</li><li>Experiencia en metodologías ágiles.</li><li>Capacidad de leer y analizar datos de producto de forma autónoma — SQL básico o experiencia con herramientas tipo Metabase, Looker o similares es un diferencial.</li><li>Curiosidad genuina por IA aplicada a productos y su uso de manera a optimizar flujos</li><li>Comunicación clara con perfiles muy distintos: desde un cocinero que usa la app hasta el CTO.</li><li>Alta tolerancia a la ambigüedad — en una startup en crecimiento, los problemas no vienen bien definidos.</li><li>Orientación a resultados: no te conformás con lanzar, te importa si el feature se usa y si resuelve el problema.</li><li>Capacidad de priorizar con criterio cuando todo parece urgente.</li><li>Habilidad para gestionar múltiples stakeholders y proyectos.</li></ul><p><br></p><p><strong>Requerimientos</strong></p><ul><li>+5 años de experiencia en roles similares</li><li>Carrera de grado o licenciatura (Admin de Empresas, Ingeniería, Marketing)</li><li>Inglés básico.</li><li>Portugués básico deseable.</li></ul><p><br></p><p><strong>Beneficios</strong></p><ul><li>Salarios competitivos internacionalmente.</li><li>Opciones en la modalidad de contratación.</li><li>Cobertura de salud dependiendo de la modalidad.</li><li>Trabajo remoto, presencial o mixto.</li><li>Feriados locales + día de cumpleaños libre + días hábiles de vacaciones.</li><li>Capacitación Inglés / Portugués in company.</li><li>Cobertura de Wellhub, para que entrenes cuando y donde sea.</li><li>Beneficios adicionales por partnerships con otras empresas</li></ul>

title: Product Owner Senior
description: En Tecnosoftware nos encontramos en la búsqueda de un/a Product Owner Senior con sólida experiencia en Mercado de Capitales, para incorporarse a un importante proyecto estratégico dentro del sector financiero. MISIÓN DEL ROL El Product Owner (PO) es responsable de maximizar el valor de un producto digital dentro del ecosistema Fintech y de mercado de capitales. Combina visión de negocio, entendimiento profundo del dominio financiero y dominio de prácticas modernas de desarrollo —incluyendo Spec-Driven Development (SDD) y el uso intensivo de Inteligencia Artificial— para acelerar el descubrimiento, la definición y la entrega de soluciones que resuelvan necesidades reales de usuarios e inversores, cumpliendo con los estándares regulatorios y de seguridad del sector. RESPONSABILIDADES Estrategia y Discovery de producto Definir y comunicar una visión de producto clara, alineada al negocio, a los usuarios y a las oportunidades del mercado de capitales. Construir y mantener el roadmap, priorizando por valor, riesgo, esfuerzo y cumplimiento regulatorio. Liderar el discovery continuo: entrevistas, análisis de datos, benchmarking competitivo y validación de hipótesis. Especificación con enfoque SDD (Spec-Driven Development) Traducir necesidades de negocio en especificaciones ejecutables, precisas y versionadas, que funcionen como única fuente de verdad para el equipo y para agentes de IA. Escribir criterios de aceptación, reglas de negocio y edge cases con el nivel de detalle que exige un producto financiero (por ej. cálculo de PPC/WAC, valuación, márgenes, settlement). Mantener las specs vivas y trazables durante todo el ciclo, asegurando que el desarrollo —con o sin asistencia de IA— refleje fielmente la intención. IA como palanca de productividad y de producto Utilizar herramientas de IA para acelerar research, síntesis de feedback, generación y refinamiento de historias/specs, prototipado y análisis de datos. Identificar y priorizar oportunidades de incorporar IA en el producto (asistentes, automatizaciones, scoring, detección de anomalías, etc.). Evaluar críticamente los outputs de IA: validar exactitud, sesgos, seguridad y cumplimiento antes de llevarlos a producción. Delivery y colaboración con el equipo Gestionar y priorizar el backlog garantizando un flujo de trabajo claro y sin bloqueos. Colaborar estrechamente con desarrollo, QA, diseño, riesgos y compliance para asegurar entregas de calidad. Participar activamente en las ceremonias ágiles y remover impedimentos. Datos, métricas y cumplimiento Definir métricas de éxito (North Star, KPIs de negocio y de producto) y monitorear su evolución. Tomar decisiones basadas en datos y en resultados de experimentos (A/B testing). Asegurar que el producto cumpla requisitos regulatorios, de seguridad y de auditoría del sector financiero. Gestión de stakeholders Comunicar visión, avances y trade-offs a áreas de negocio, tecnología y gerencia. Alinear expectativas y negociar prioridades con transparencia. CONOCIMIENTOS REQUERIDOS Metodologías y prácticas modernas Metodologías ágiles: Scrum, Kanban. Spec-Driven Development (SDD): escritura de especificaciones claras, testeables y aptas para desarrollo asistido por IA. Gestión de producto: estrategia, priorización, roadmapping y discovery. Inteligencia Artificial aplicada Uso de asistentes de IA (LLMs) para productividad y para el proceso de producto. Nociones de prompt engineering y evaluación crítica de outputs. Comprensión general de capacidades y límites de la IA (deseable: GenAI, RAG, agentes). Dominio Fintech / Mercado de Capitales Instrumentos y operatoria: renta fija/variable, FX, derivados, FCI, cauciones. Procesos: pricing/valuación, liquidación (settlement), custodia, reporting y P&L. Marco regulatorio y de compliance (deseable: CNV, BCRA, PLA/FT, seguridad de la información). Técnicos de producto Definición y documentación de requisitos, historias de usuario y criterios de aceptación. Principios de UX/UI (deseable Figma). Análisis de datos para la toma de decisiones. HABILIDADES Y COMPETENCIAS Pensamiento crítico: capacidad de cuestionar propuestas de forma constructiva y proponer alternativas superadoras. Comunicación clara adaptada a distintas audiencias (técnicas y de negocio). Priorización y toma de decisiones bajo incertidumbre. Colaboración y liderazgo sin autoridad formal. Orientación a datos y a resultados. Aprendizaje continuo y adaptabilidad ante mercados y tecnologías cambiantes. Atención al detalle y rigurosidad, crítica en productos financieros. HERRAMIENTAS Gestión de producto y backlog: Jira, Confluence, Trello / Linear. IA y productividad: ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot y herramientas de SDD (deseable: Cursor, GitHub Spec Kit o similares). Comunicación: Slack, Zoom, Google Meet. Diseño: Figma (deseable, no excluyente). Analítica de datos: Google Analytics / Tag Manager / Looker Studio / SQL (deseable, no excluyente). EXPERIENCIA Experiencia comprobable como Product Owner o rol similar (excluyente). Experiencia trabajando con metodologías ágiles (excluyente). Experiencia en productos digitales, idealmente en Fintech, banca o mercado de capitales (altamente valorada). Experiencia utilizando IA en el flujo de trabajo de producto (diferencial). COMPETENCIAS PERSONALES Orientación al cliente y al negocio. Pensamiento estratégico y crítico. Liderazgo e influencia. Flexibilidad y adaptabilidad. Autonomía y proactividad. Motivación por el logro y resiliencia en entornos desafiantes. Modalidad hibrida, asistencia 2 o 3 veces por semana en Retiro, CABA. Beneficios Relación de dependencia con Tecnosoftware. Prepaga Swiss Medical Group para grupo familiar primario (hasta 3 cápitas). Día libre de cumpleaños. Medio día libre por cumpleaños de hijo/a. Reintegro del 50% en vacunación de mascotas. Descuentos en UADE, UAI y Universidad Siglo XXI. Descuentos en Educación IT y CUI. Beneficios en BGH, Sony y Finaer.

celebrate in style with friends and family.</li></ul><p><br></p><p><strong>About the project:</strong></p><p><br></p><p>As a <strong>Senior Product Manager</strong>, you will drive initiatives related objectives.</p><p><br></p><p><strong>What you’ll do:</strong></p><p><br></p><ul><li>Lead and coordinate event program operations, ensuring digital initiatives are executed efficiently across event iterate on event strategies.</li><li>Collaborate with data and analytics teams to identify attendee segments, engagement patterns, and experience profile data opportunities that inform personalization and targeting decisions.</li><li>Support roadmap development and feature prioritization for event platforms (RainFocus, Swoogo, On24, AEM), balancing attendee needs, business value, and technical feasibility.</li><li>Serve as a senior point of contact for internal stakeholders and event clients, managing expectations and communicating proactively on program status, platform health, and feature readiness.</li></ul><p><br></p><p><strong>What makes you a great fit:</strong></p><p><br></p><ul><li>Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.</li><li>5+ Years of experience working in Product Management, Product Operations, or Program Design Operations.</li><li>Experience leading initiatives across design, product, engineering, QA, and data teams.</li><li>Experience working with design systems and multidisciplinary digital product teams.</li><li>Familiarity with Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) or similar CMS platforms with component-based architectures.</li><li>Experience collaborating with engineering teams in Agile/Scrum environments.</li><li>Understanding of A/B testing, experimentation workflows, and personalization initiatives.</li><li>Advanced English Level is required for this role, as you will work with US clients. Effective communication in English is essential to deliver the best solutions to our clients and expand your horizons.</li></ul><p><br></p><p><strong>Global Impact, Local Culture 🌍 </strong></p><p><br></p><p>For over 25 years, we’ve been shaping digital transformation, delivering complex solutions for global enterprises and public sector organizations. Today, we are at the forefront of an AI-driven transformation era, helping organizations turn data into real business value. By combining deep domain expertise with data and AI, we design solutions that create immediate impact while scaling for the future.</p><p><br></p><p>We believe complexity doesn’t have to mean complicated, and that the best solutions are those that work in the real world, not just on paper. title: Senior Product Manager, Data & Solution Strategy
description: At ASAPP, our mission is simple: deliver the best AI-powered customer experience—faster than anyone else. To achieve that, we’re guided by principles that shape how we think, build, and execute. We value customer obsession, purposeful speed, ownership, and a relentless focus on outcomes. We work in tight, skilled teams, prioritize clarity over complexity, and continuously evolve through curiosity, data, and craftsmanship. We’re seeking technologists and problem solvers who thrive in fast-paced environments, love collaborating with great talent, and approach every day like it’s Day 1. We're a globally diverse team with hubs in New York City, Mountain View, Latin America, and India. If you're driven by continuous learning, rapid pivots, and the challenges of building in a high-growth startup, we’d love to talk. This is more than a job—it’s a journey. This is not a reporting role. You will own the data layer that makes ASAPP's platform trustworthy and actionable — the models, dashboards, feeds, and APIs that let builders, supervisors, analysts, and executives at our customers see exactly what GenerativeAgent (GA) is doing, how well it's doing it, and its value. If customers can't see the value we create, they can't renew, expand, or defend the investment internally. That visibility is your product. What You Will Do Drive the roadmap for customer-facing dashboards and analytics. Lead product for surfaces like the Supervisor homepage and dashboards, that let supervisors break down GA performance by custom questions, quality signals, containment, escalation, and resolution metrics. Balance depth for power users with clarity for first-time users. Build the value realization story. Translate raw platform data into the metrics that prove ROI — containment, escalation rate, verified resolution rate, ASAPP Score, CSAT — and partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Analytics to package these into narratives customers can bring to their own leadership. Own exportable data feeds and real-time data APIs. Design and manage the feeds and APIs that let customers pull ASAPP data into their own BI stacks and data warehouses. Treat schema changes, naming, and versioning as customer commitments, not implementation details. Own the data strategy layer. title: Product Owner - Data Intelligence
description: The job can be based in Poland, Portugal or Agentina. MAKE HISTORY WITH US At PMI, we’ve chosen to do something incredible. We’re totally transforming our business and building our future on smoke-free products with the power to deliver a smoke-free future. With huge change, comes huge opportunity. So, wherever you join us, you’ll enjoy the freedom to dream up and deliver better, brighter solutions and you will have the space to move your career forward in many different areas/directions. The Product Owner - Data Intelligence Platform is accountable for the vision, roadmap and maximizing business value from the platforms enabling Generative AI, Agentic AI, and Advanced AI/ML capabilities across the company. The role owns what problems are worth solving, why they matter, and how platform capabilities translate into measurable outcomes. This role sits at the intersection of business demand, technology, governance, and adoption, ensuring that investment in Generative AI, Agentic AI, and Advanced Analytics results in real customer value, responsible scale, and sustainable cost and risk management. The Product Owner acts as a steward of value and a strategic integrator, ensuring teams focus on well-defined, high‑impact problems while avoiding misaligned use cases and uncontrolled experimentation, and while effectively managing and collaborating with stakeholders. Product Scope The role owns the product vision and value delivery for PMI’s Data Intelligence platform, including: Generative AI Platforms - enterprise LLM access (AWS Bedrock, Gemini and Azure), GenAI APIs, knowledge bases, guardrails. GenAI Playgrounds – Custom inhouse development solutions to promote AI fluency within the company. Agentic AI Enablement LangSmith, LangGraph, Databricks, AgentCore – runtime, observability, and evaluation of agent-based workflows. Advanced Analytics & AI/ML Platforms Databricks, Amazon SageMaker – end to end platform for model development, training, deployment, MLOps, and governance These platforms are treated as enterprise products—designed for reuse, scale, governance, and long‑term business impact. JOIN US WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 4+ years in Product Management / Product Ownership, preferably for platforms Proven experience with GenAI, AI/ML, or advanced analytics ecosystems Strong background in Agile, product‑centric operating models Solid understanding of: Generative AI and LLM ecosystems Agentic AI and orchestration patterns AI/ML lifecycle, AIOps and MLOps Working knowledge of GenAI, Agentic AI, ML technologies (i.e. AWS Bedrock, GCP, Azure, AWS Sagemaker, Databricks, OpenAI, Langchain) Understanding of IT Platform building principles (Microservices Architecture, CI/CD, Scalability, multitenancy) Comfortable operating in large, regulated enterprise environments Strong understanding of Agile principles and practices, particularly in the context of the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe), Scrum and Kanban Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams and stakeholders Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to prioritize and make trade-offs based on business value WHAT WE OFFER YOU? Our Success Depends On The Men And Women Who Come To Work Every Single Day With a Sense Of Purpose And An Appetite For Progress. Join PMI And You Too Can Seize the freedom to define your future and ours. We’ll empower you to take risks, experiment, and explore. Be part of an inclusive, diverse culture, where everyone’s contribution is respected; collaborate with some of the world’s best people and feel like you belong. Pursue your ambitions and develop your skills with a global business – our staggering size and scale provide endless opportunities to progress. Take pride in delivering our promise to society to deliver a smoke-free future. In case of being hired in Poland in this position you will earn no less than PLN 21 800 gross per month HOW CAN YOU MAKE HISTORY WITH US? Own the product vision, roadmap, and backlog with explicit linkage to business outcomes, value realization, adoption, and customer satisfaction Prioritize initiatives based on expected value, strategic relevance, feasibility, and risk, continuously challenging solution‑first thinking with clear problem statements and success criteria Represent the needs of business users, data scientists, engineers, and platform consumers, ensuring platforms remove friction and enable meaningful outcomes Drive structured feedback loops (user engagement, NPS/CSAT, usage data) and translate insights into evidence‑based roadmap decisions Act as a trusted partner to senior stakeholders, translating complex technical or regulatory constraints into clear, decision‑ready trade‑offs and managing cross‑team dependencies Lead the evolution of secure, scalable, and compliant platforms, embedding Responsible AI, security, privacy, and compliance by design Embrace continuous discovery and problem framing, validating who benefits, how success is measured, and whether a platform solution is justified before scaling Partner with engineering to ensure high‑quality delivery, transparent governance, KPI tracking (value, usage, cost), and clear communication of progress, risks, and decisions Please note that only on-line applications will be taken into consideration. Each person who sends the application will receive information about its status. Relocation support is not available. At PMI we run the business in line with ethical principles and encourage SpeakUp culture. We care for equal chances and fair treatment. If you find anything that violates these principles in this job offer or the recruitment process, you may contact our Ethics and Compliance Team at PMIEthicsandCompliance@pmi.com . Read more about Ethics&Compliance at PMI – here. 27040

title: Product Manager, Laravel Cloud
description: Laravel is the most popular PHP framework in the world. 500M+ lifetime downloads. Thousands of packages. A developer community that shows up — at conferences, in forums, on Twitter, in Discord servers, and in every "what framework should I use?" thread on the internet. But Laravel is more than a framework. It is a complete ecosystem with dedicated tools and resources to help you go from building an app locally to deploying it, monitoring usage, and then improving and scaling it up. Laravel Cloud is the platform at heart of it all: a fully managed home for web apps, with managed compute, databases, caches, object storage, WebSockets, queues, and built-in scale-to-zero with millisecond wakes that keeps idle infrastructure from breaking the budget. We're early. Laravel Cloud is growing fast, the roadmap is wide open, and the decisions we make now will shape the product for years. There is no 50-page process doc and no layer of approvals between you and shipping. What there is: incredible product-market fit, a brand that opens every door, and a small team of people who care deeply about doing this right. We're looking for a Product Manager to help us build it. Why this role is unique You are building infrastructure for developers with strong, informed opinions and a low tolerance for inauthenticity Earning technical credibility matters, even if you are not an engineer — you'll be making product calls about compute, databases, and scaling You own a real slice of the product end to end and operate in real ambiguity, helping define what Laravel Cloud becomes Product is a team sport here. Engineering, design, and marketing are true partners What you will do Own products end-to-end. Take an area of Laravel Cloud from conception to launch — discovery, prioritization, and shipping — and know it better than anyone in the company Partner closely with engineering. Define scope and appetite together with engineering, bringing the why, the who, and the when while the team owns the how Stay close to customers. Talk to customers regularly — enterprise calls, community signal, direct interviews — and let what you learn drive prioritization Be data-driven on outcomes. "We shipped it" isn't the finish line — adoption is. Track how features are adopted and used, and prioritize based on what the data says Be the connective tissue. Brief marketing and sales ahead of launches and own the holistic experience, so your area feels coherent, not just complete What the ideal candidate brings Good taste and a high craft bar. You have opinions about what makes product feel right and defend them, holding design and engineering to a high standard Focus on what matters. Comfortable juggling several projects at once, with ruthless prioritization and clear async communication Competitive awareness. You know the landscape cold — Heroku, Vercel, Railway, Render, Fly — and what good looks like on observability, deploy ergonomics, and billing transparency Technical curiosity. Learns infrastructure concepts proactively to maintain credibility with technical audiences Customer-first, collaborative DNA. Strong cross-functional partnerships, with a focus on developer value over shipping features Comfort with early-stage ambiguity. Enjoys experimentation and iteration, and building the plane while flying it What success looks like Velocity. You ship fast and on time — speed is core to how we work, and PMs have outsized impact on it Quality. You ship with the level of quality synonymous with Laravel, scoping with engineering so work lands well the first time Outcomes. Your area is adopted and your customers are satisfied — not just launched Requirements Minimum qualifications Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience 4 years of experience in product management or a related technical role 2 years of experience taking technical products from conception to launch (0 to 1, ideation through execution) Experience developing or launching infrastructure products or technologies — compute, databases, storage, networking, file systems, or other software infrastructure Preferred qualifications Experience with cloud, platform-as-a-service, or developer-tools products Familiarity with Laravel, PHP, or modern web application development Experience working cross-functionally with engineering, design, marketing, and other stakeholders Comfort working closely with engineering to shape scope, in a fast-moving, async-first environment Background in software development or engineering Benefits Fully remote, globally distributed team Option to attend Laracon conferences around the world Paid time off (vacation, sick leave, public holidays) Family leave (maternity, paternity) Company equity Access to high quality training tools to ensure you are enabled to be the best you can be Welcome kit with custom Laravel swag

description: At INDI, we're passionate about empowering individuals and businesses worldwide. Our cutting-edge recruiters connect leading companies with top talent, fostering a dynamic environment where innovation thrives. Join us in shaping the future of work. As a Product Owner, you will play a critical and active role in the day-to-day operations. Key responsibilities: - Create and maintain robust product roadmaps and backlogs create features/epics and user stories. Requirements: - Solid experience in similar roles. - 2 + years of experience as Agile Product Owner. - 2+ years of experience as business analysis: capturing functional requirements, understanding user pain points. - Additional experience either as a Project Manager or Software Developer. - Experience in product development, from design to testing. - Experience with both learning existing products, or building them from scratch. - Results oriented with negotiation skills and good communication. - Advanced English level. This innovation empowers users worldwide to monetize everyday mobile activities such as streaming, gaming, and shopping. We enable users to profit from their data and attention, rather than letting only tech giants benefit. What sets us apart is our inclusive approach, converting users into earners, facilitating over $150M in earnings and savings, and going a step further by turning earners into owners by awarding stock ownership in Mode.Inc based on their usage. We have attracted over 40 million users across 170 countries. Mode Mobile, Inc. Ranked Number 1 Fastest Growing Company in North America on the 2023 Deloitte Technology Fast 500. For additional insights, check out information about our reward-based super app, Mode Earn App, which also powers the reward engine for our proprietary smartphone, Mode Earn Phone. Our Team and Culture Drive Our Success Our team is the heart of our culture. We value innovation, collaboration, and curiosity, with a passion for getting things done. We strive to hire and cultivate the best team members and foster a culture of open communication and transparency. We are driven and hard-working but also committed to having fun along the way. We allow OKRs to guide us, assume positive intent, sometimes agree to disagree and commit, honor our commitments, seek to accomplish more with less, and encourage everyone to speak up as our team owns our company's success. title: Senior Technical Product Manager, Banking Platform
description: The salary range for this role is $5,000 - $8,000 per month (Gross in USD) About Sezzle: With a mission to financially empower the next generation, Sezzle is revolutionizing the shopping experience beyond payments, blending cutting-edge tech with seamless, interest-free installment plans that make shopping smarter and more accessible. We’re not just transforming payments; we’re redefining how people discover, interact with, and purchase the things they love while driving real impact on merchant sales through increased conversions and higher order values. As we continue to shape the future of fintech and retail, we’re building an innovative, dynamic team passionate about creating more than just a transaction but a truly unique shopping journey. If you’re excited about pushing boundaries in tech and delivering a game-changing experience for consumers and merchants alike, come join us at Sezzle and help create the future of shopping! About the Role: We are seeking a talented and motivated Senior Technical Product Manager who is best in class with a high IQ plus a high EQ. This role presents an exciting opportunity to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment within a rapidly growing team, with abundant prospects for career advancement. Sezzle is building the platform that will carry us from a BNPL provider into a full-stack financial institution. This role owns the system at the center of that: Sezzle’s banking core — the ledger, accounts and balances, and the money movement that every future Sezzle financial product will run on. You would own it end to end. Discovery, architecture and vendor decisions, requirements, build, launch, and everything after — not a slice of someone else’s roadmap, but the full product lifecycle for the platform itself. You’d work directly with Engineering, Finance, Compliance, Treasury, and Risk, with real authority over how this gets built. Ideally you’ve built something like this before. If you haven’t, but you’ve owned a ledger, a payments platform, an issuing program, or other financial infrastructure — and you’re the kind of person who learns a domain properly rather than around the edges — we want to talk to you. What matters most is that you’ve owned real infrastructure and that you’re willing to go deep on the parts you don’t know yet. What You'll Do: Own the banking platform roadmap. Define and sequence the platform work required to support accounts, deposits, cards, and lending on a single ledger and account model. Help drive the build-vs-buy decision. Evaluate core banking platforms and processors, run vendor diligence, model cost and time-to-market, and help leadership decide whether we extend what we have or integrate a third party. Shape the account and ledger model. Work with Engineering and Finance on account hierarchies, sub-ledgers, chart-of-accounts mapping, posting rules, holds, interest and fee accrual, and general ledger integration. Specify money movement. Own product requirements for transfers, ACH, card issuing and network settlement, real-time rails, and returns and reversals — including exception handling, cutoff windows, and settlement reconciliation. Make the platform auditable. Ensure the system produces the reporting, traceability, and controls that Finance, audit, and regulators need — reconciliation breaks, balance attestation, and complete transaction history. Partner on regulatory readiness. Work with Compliance and Legal to turn their requirements into platform capabilities: screening hooks, onboarding data, error resolution, disclosures and statements, and reporting. You don’t need to arrive fluent in US banking regulation — you do need to be someone who learns it properly. Plan migration and cutover. If a migration is in scope, own data mapping, parallel-run strategy, validation criteria, rollback plans, and phased cutover. Write the technical requirements. Own detailed specs, API contracts, event schemas, data models, user stories, and release plans end-to-end. Use data to prove it works. Write your own SQL. Define platform KPIs — posting latency, reconciliation break rate, settlement accuracy, failure rates — and monitor them relentlessly. Manage risk early. Anticipate technical risks, edge cases, race conditions, and dependencies before they become incidents. Money movement defects are the expensive kind. Operate with urgency. Deliver against an evolving regulatory and business timeline with incomplete information. What We Look For: Bachelor’s or advanced degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or other technical discipline (required). 5–10 years of product experience, with meaningful time spent on financial infrastructure rather than only customer-facing surfaces. Real ownership in at least one of the following. You do not need all of them, and we care much more about depth in one than exposure to several: Ledgers, general ledger, or balance and transaction systems Payments processing, orchestration, or money movement — ACH, card networks, transfers, settlement, or the LATAM equivalents (PIX, SPEI, PSE, CCE) Card issuing or card program management Deposit, wallet, or account platforms Lending origination or loan servicing platforms Product work at a processor, BaaS provider, or core banking vendor Comfort with double-entry accounting concepts as they show up in software — debits and credits, sub-ledgers, accruals, reconciliation — or a genuine appetite to get comfortable with them quickly. Deep technical understanding of APIs, event-driven architecture, idempotency, distributed system failure modes, batch vs. real-time processing, and data flows. Strong SQL skills and comfort querying and interpreting data independently. Experience working directly with Compliance, Legal, Finance, or Treasury as stakeholders — not only Engineering and Design. Comfortable working in ambiguity and making sound, documented decisions with incomplete information. Strong written and verbal communication — can hold your own in an engineering standup, a Finance review, and an executive discussion. Hands-on familiarity with AI tools, data models, or generative AI applications—personally, professionally, or better yet, both! Preferred Qualifications: Direct experience with a core banking platform, in-house or vendor (Thought Machine, Mambu, 10x, Finxact, Temenos, Technisys, Galileo, Pismo, or similar). Experience with a core migration, conversion, or major ledger replacement. Experience at a chartered or licensed financial institution, or supporting a charter, banking licence, or deposit insurance application. Familiarity with consumer finance regulation — US (Reg E, Reg DD, Reg CC, Reg Z, TILA, FCRA, BSA/AML) or equivalent local regimes. Background in consumer credit or BNPL, card products, or bank-fintech sponsorship programs. Experience with third-party risk management and vendor oversight in a regulated environment. About You: You have relentlessly high standards - many people may think your standards are unreasonably high. You are continually raising the bar and driving those around you to deliver great results. You make sure that defects do not get sent down the line and that problems are fixed so they stay fixed. You’re not bound by convention - your success—and much of the fun—lies in developing new ways to do things You need action - speed matters in business. Many decisions and actions are reversible and do not need extensive study. We value calculated risk-taking. You earn trust - you listen attentively, speak candidly, and treat others respectfully. You have backbone; disagree, then commit - you can respectfully challenge decisions when you disagree, even when doing so is uncomfortable or exhausting. You have conviction and are tenacious. You do not compromise for the sake of social cohesion. Once a decision is determined, you commit wholly. You deliver results - you focus on the key inputs and deliver them with the right quality and in a timely fashion. Despite setbacks, you rise to the occasion and never settle. What Makes Working at Sezzle Awesome: At Sezzle, we are more than just brilliant engineers, passionate data enthusiasts, out-of-the-box thinkers, and determined innovators. We believe in surrounding ourselves with only the best and the brightest individuals. Our culture is not defined by a certain set of perks designed to give the illusion of the traditional startup culture, but rather, it is the visible example living in every employee that we hire. #Full-time

title: Senior Product Manager
description: Team : Product Reports to : CTO & CPO Works closely with: CMO, Head of AI, UX Director, Engineering, Business development, Business intelligence, Clinical team, and genetic counselor. Why This Role Exists A mother notices that her two-year-old is developing differently than the children she sees on the playground. She brings it up at the next well-child visit. The pediatrician has fifteen minutes, a growth chart, a vaccine schedule, and a full waiting room. The concern is real and the visit is short, and what happens next depends almost entirely on how well that concern gets translated into something a clinical system can act on. That translation is our product. Family Health Checker lets the family prepare before the doctor visit — symptoms, photos, family history—and hands the clinician something structured instead of an incomplete story told from memory. Face2Gene receives the case information from Family Health Checker—it helps the clinician review the phenotype findings, contextualize symptoms and HPOs, consider relevant syndromes and genes — cutting the time needed to prepare the clinical documentation that a referral or a lab test order actually needs. There is a second, quieter failure this role exists to prevent. A health system agrees to a deployment in March, and by August nothing has been turned on, because nobody decided who sends the invitation before the visit or who acts on the output when it arrives. The product worked. The pathway never existed. Building and growing these products is the job. You will be the person who decides what our products do, what they are allowed to claim, how a clinical insight earns a clinician's attention, and how a family moves from a first concern to a real next step. You will not do it alone—our clinical, medical, and technology teams are there with you—but you will own it in the product, every day. We are a small company, and that shapes the role in two ways. The surface is wide: you will touch the family experience, the clinician experience, deployment, and measurement, without a large product organization around you. In exchange you get the whole problem rather than a slice of it, and decisions that take a quarter somewhere else take a week here. Working with Our Clinical Team You do not have to be a clinician to do this job well. Our Chief Medical Officer, our clinical team, and our genetic counselor are the clinical expertise, and they are close at hand. What we need from you is the ability to take a clinical question to the right person, ask it precisely, listen carefully, and turn the answer into a product decision rather than a meeting note. A clinical background is genuinely welcome, and it will make parts of this easier. It is desired but not a requirement. Curiosity, care with detail, and a habit of checking rather than assuming will get you far. What You Will Own Face2Gene - Clinician Decision Support Clinical decision support layer: How the product helps a clinician understand why a case merits further review, referral, testing, follow-up, or reassurance, and how prioritized genes, syndrome considerations, and phenotype findings are presented for clinician review. Report credibility layer: Showing which inputs drove a finding—photo-analysis-AI supported phenotype signals, symptoms, developmental observations—with source tags a clinician can inspect. Skeptical-clinician language mode: Clinical, evidence-aware wording used when a parent-originated summary reaches a clinician, so the first impression is a structured case rather than an app result. Pediatrician speed mode: A workflow that fits within a short visit and does not require the clinician to be a geneticist. Family Health Checker - The Family Experience Parent-facing result language: Educational, useful without being alarming, and explicitly not a diagnosis. User guidance & safety: Photo guidance, consent moments, and managing points in the flow where a family is most anxious. Escalation messaging: Next-step language that clearly directs a family on what actions to take. Next-gen features: Help develop the next generation of visual-AI results, symptoms, and health history assessment. Pathway, Deployment, and Integration Family Health Checker to Face2Gene handoff: Turning what a family entered into a package a clinician can work from, rather than a consumer report a clinician has to re-enter. Share and open rates are a product problem, not a marketing one. Digital front door: Making Family Health Checker straightforward for a health system to send before visits, embed in a portal, deploy by QR code in a waiting room, and white-label. Integration surface: PDF and structured export, FHIR document exchange, single sign-on, and the Epic pathway—working with engineering on what we build and with the health system on what they configure. Non-code deployment factors: Who owns the invitation, who acts on the output, what the security and privacy review will ask for, and how a Phase 1 is scoped so it can be measured without disrupting a stretched team. Routing and documentation: Configurable next steps across pediatrics, developmental pediatrics, genetics, telehealth, testing, and follow-up, with referral packets, draft letters of medical necessity, ICD-10 support, and requisition readiness as drafts for clinician review and editing. Laboratory ordering: Integrations and buyer logic that go with lab orders (distinct from health-system buyer logic). Evidence, Quality, and Measurement Review representation: Representing product in clinical and regulatory review, user experience and usability testing, and AI model performance gates. Evidence standards: Defining the evidence bar for a claim before it appears in the product, and working with our AI and validation lead on what has to be measured before we can say something. Metrics & instrumentation: The metric tree from intake completion through clinician action to outcome capture, the instrumentation behind it, and dashboards a health system can read without asking us. Post-market business intelligence: Model alignment, escalation routing behavior, and user experience that has drifted outside its usefulness, friendliness, or compliance boundary. Advisory relationships: Engaging with clinical advisory and design partners to turn feedback into concrete product decisions. Your First Year First 60 days: You have studied the workflows used by general and developmental pediatricians, and geneticists, and can describe the pathway from parent concern to next-step action in your own words. You have audited every parent-facing and clinician-facing screen against our user audiences and produced a prioritized list of potential gaps. You know the three places the pathway most often breaks. By 4 months: The product and engineering team has delivered an improvement you designed. A Phase 1 deployment is running with named metrics and a named owner on the other side. The clinical review has a defined, documented process with you being a part of it. By 9 months: A skeptical pediatrician who has never met us can use one of our products and understand within a minute what it is, what it is not, and what to do next. A new health system can go from agreement to live use on a documented path with a predictable calendar. The evidence bar for our clinical claims is enforced while providing a smooth user experience. Required What We Are Looking For Product Experience: 4+ years in product management, including at least one product owned from definition through to live use with real users. You remember what it cost to get it there. Healthcare Domain Knowledge: Working knowledge of healthcare. You have built software used in a clinical, diagnostic, or patient-facing setting, or can show that you learn a regulated, high-stakes domain quickly and enjoy doing it. Why This Role Exists A mother notices that her two-year-old is developing differently than the children she sees on the playground. She brings it up at the next well-child visit. The pediatrician has fifteen minutes, a growth chart, a vaccine schedule, and a full waiting room. The concern is real and the visit is short, and what happens next depends almost entirely on how well that concern gets translated into something a clinical system can act on. That translation is our product. Family Health Checker lets the family prepare before the doctor visit — symptoms, photos, family history—and hands the clinician something structured instead of an incomplete story told from memory. Face2Gene receives the case information from Family Health Checker—it helps the clinician review the phenotype findings, contextualize symptoms and HPOs, consider relevant syndromes and genes — cutting the time needed to prepare the clinical documentation that a referral or a lab test order actually needs. There is a second, quieter failure this role exists to prevent. A health system agrees to a deployment in March, and by August nothing has been turned on, because nobody decided who sends the invitation before the visit or who acts on the output when it arrives. The product worked. The pathway never existed. Building and growing these products is the job. You will be the person who decides what our products do, what they are allowed to claim, how a clinical insight earns a clinician's attention, and how a family moves from a first concern to a real next step. You will not do it alone—our clinical, medical, and technology teams are there with you—but you will own it in the product, every day. We are a small company, and that shapes the role in two ways.
